draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Changanassery! Out on the Vazhoor road there's a church that's the only one in Asia with St Maurus as its patron saint, and his relics were brought all the way from Italy.
draft.hungryLine: This is Central Travancore, a meat lover's region of spicy chicken, beef, mutton and pork dishes shaped by Nasrani Christian cooking.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Drive out along the Changanacherry-Vazhoor Road through Mammood to Karukachal and the church at Koothrapally.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: The villages around here, like Perumpanachy and Mammood, are all rubber, paddy fields, coconut trees and pepper.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Karukachal gets its name from karuka grass, which grew in plenty, and chal, a small stream of flowing water.

spots.name: St. Mary's Syro Malabar Catholic Church, Koothrapally
spots.detail: Short drive · Founded in 1876, home of the St Maurus statue

spots.name: Karukachal
spots.detail: 14 km away · A fast-growing town on the Vazhoor road

spots.name: Perumpanachy
spots.detail: 6 km away · Green village of rubber, paddy and pepper

legends.title: The monk who saved a friend
legends.body: St Maurus, the first disciple of St Benedict, is famous for rescuing his fellow monk St Placidus from drowning. Devotees here call him Vishuda Maurus Muthapan.

legends.title: Named for grass and water
legends.body: Karukachal was named after the karuka grass that grew here in plenty and a small flowing stream. The name has stuck as the town grew.

tips.title: Catch Muthappan Perunnal.
tips.body: The feast of St Maurus at Koothrapally falls in the week of the Epiphany season, with Pindikuthi Perunnal as part of it.

tips.title: Brace for spice.
tips.body: Central Travancore sits in the spice belt, so most dishes are extremely spicy.

story.title: Karuka grass by the stream
story.body: Karukachal took its name from the grass that grew in plenty and a small body of flowing water.

story.title: Veliyachan's church
story.body: Palakunnel Mathai Mariam Kathanar, known as Palakunnel Veliyachan, founded the church at Koothrapally. He is remembered for his struggles for the Dalit community in the 19th century.

story.title: Relics from Italy
story.body: Veliyachan brought relics of St Maurus from Italy and installed his statue in the chapel. It is the only church in Asia with St Maurus as patron.

story.title: Rubber and paddy country
story.body: The villages around Changanassery are green with rubber plantations, paddy fields, coconut and pepper. The Changanacherry-Vazhoor Road, almost a century old, still links them.
